Storm Hit Your Roof? Start With This Checklist

A free, printable two-page checklist for the hours, days and weeks after a Houston hailstorm or windstorm. Fill in the short form and it opens straight away.

Call (832) 662-4107 Get the checklist
  1. Home
  2. Storm Claim Checklist

Two printed pages for the days after a storm

After hail, wind or a tropical storm, the first few days decide a lot: what gets photographed, whether more water gets in, which contractor you trust, and whether the claim is filed in time.

The checklist puts all of that on two pages you can print and keep in a drawer before the next storm season. Fill in the form and it opens straight away.

Your details are not sold. See the privacy policy.

What the checklist covers

  1. Right after the storm. Power line safety, staying off the roof, and writing down the date, time and hail size.
  2. Documenting the damage. The photos that matter, including gutters, vents, air conditioner fins and screens that show hail size.
  3. Stopping more damage. Buckets, moving belongings, having a roofer tarp an open roof, and keeping every receipt.
  4. Your policy. Percentage deductibles, replacement cost versus actual cash value, and reporting deadlines.
  5. Filing and the adjuster's visit. Why it helps to have the roofer on the roof when the adjuster comes.
  6. Hiring safely. Insurance certificates, a written scope, deposits, and the Texas rule against waiving deductibles.
  7. After the work. Invoices, permits, warranties and asking the insurer to release any held-back depreciation.

Print it before the next storm

Atlantic hurricane season runs from June 1 to November 30, and Houston's spring thunderstorms bring hail and straight-line wind of their own. When a storm hits a whole region, roofers book up quickly and door-knockers arrive within days. A list you read in advance makes those days calmer.

For more depth, see storm damage roof repair, the storm damage steps guide and the roof insurance claims guide.

The deductible is yours to pay. The Texas Department of Insurance says it is illegal for a contractor to offer to waive, rebate or absorb your deductible, and a contract of $1,000 or more paid with insurance money must include a notice saying so. A roofer also may not act as your public adjuster on a property it works on. Treat any offer to "cover the deductible" as a reason to call someone else.

Stay off the roof. Wet, storm-damaged roofs are slick and the decking may be weak, so leave the ladder in the garage. Keep well away from downed power lines and report them to CenterPoint Energy or 911. Indoors, move belongings away from the leak, put a bucket or towels under the drip and keep people out of any room where the ceiling sags. Photograph the damage from the ground and inside the house, then call your insurer and a roofer.

Questions Houston homeowners ask

Is the checklist really free?

Yes. Enter your first name, email and ZIP code and it opens straight away as a PDF. There is nothing to buy.

Will someone call me if I fill in the form?

Only if you add your phone number, which asks a local roofer to call you about an inspection. Leave the phone field empty and you simply get the checklist. You can also call the line yourself at any hour.

Is this checklist legal or insurance advice?

No. It is general information for greater Houston homeowners. Your policy and your insurer have the final word on what is covered and when you must report damage. The roof insurance claims guide explains the Texas rules in more depth.

What should I photograph after hail?

From the ground only: every side of the roof, dented gutters, downspouts and roof vents, the fins on the outdoor air conditioner, window screens, and any shingle pieces or granules in the yard. Inside, every ceiling stain and wet spot, with the date. The hail damage page explains why dented metal matters.
